vqa_items.question: As a directed data-flow diagram, can a viewer visually trace every important movement from source to destination through clearly differentiated systems, processes, stores or queues, labels, arrows, and scope boundaries, with disciplined routing and professional diagram polish?

score_criteria.2: Award 2 only if the diagram is exceptionally clear and production-ready: every node, label, arrowhead, data-flow name, store or queue, and boundary is readable at normal size; direction is unmistakable end to end; node roles are visually distinct; routing is economical, balanced, and nearly free of crossings; spacing and alignment create a calm, deliberate structure; and no connector appears detached, ambiguous, broken, hidden, clipped, or visually misleading. The diagram must look deliberately engineered, not merely auto-laid-out. Any uncertainty in flow direction, role distinction, or cleanup prevents 2.
score_criteria.1: Award 1 if the main flow can be followed and the diagram is substantially usable, but it has one or more visible weaknesses such as avoidable crossings, slightly ambiguous arrows, inconsistent node shapes, dense labels, weak boundaries, uneven spacing, or a generic auto-generated appearance. It may be decent, but not exemplary.
score_criteria.0: Award 0 even if nodes and arrows are present when the diagram is visually weak enough to require major redesign: important paths are difficult to trace, arrow direction is ambiguous, connectors collide or detach, node roles are confusing, labels are too small or crowded, scope is unclear, or the layout is chaotic, crude, or misleading. Blank, corrupted, severely unreadable, or materially incomplete diagrams are also 0.
